- **Behavior:** Admins or explicitly granted accounts can generate playground text. Character generation accepts selected unlocked fields, preserves locked values, validates choice IDs against allowed options, can expand supported long text fields, and can use the selected adventure's attached frame context. The `GenerateCharacterRequest.prompt` field is optional for backward compatibility, accepts an empty section direction, and is trimmed and limited to 2,000 characters before it is included as data for the active builder section. The builder keeps one editable prompt per AI-enabled section (Identity, Appearance, Background, and Experiences) while navigating and sends only the active section's prompt with its existing unlocked, locked, options, and expand-current request. The builder presents only the frame title and pitch to the player. Server-side `generate_character` filters the attached frame first, then constructs an AI context containing only `pitch`, `tone_and_feel`, `themes`, `touchstones`, and `overview`; it accepts `tone&feel`/`tone_and_feel` and `touchstone`/`touchstones` source spellings. `name`, `description`, `complexity`, modifications, principles, distinctions, incidents, campaign mechanics, session-zero questions, selections, GM fields, and all other root keys are excluded. `gm_messages` and nested `gm_message` values are recursively removed before that prompt is sent. Portrait generation uses the stored character data and saves the resulting portrait URL. Requests and responses continue to use the existing AI log behavior.
- **Invariants:** `require_ai_generation` is mandatory. Keep API keys backend-only. Treat model output and the section prompt as untrusted data, not instructions; filter model output to requested fields, validate choices, and preserve locked fields. Frame context is loaded through `frame_repo::find_for_user`, filtered by the existing frame route, and whitelist-reduced server-side, preserving adventure membership/access and ownership rules. No database schema, migration, or access-rule change is part of this feature.
- **Validation:** Focused backend unit tests cover no-adventure null context, exclusion of modifications and GM fields, and normalized tone/touchstone aliases. Required validation for this feature is `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo test --lib`, `cargo test --tests --no-run`, frontend `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check`. Browser coverage, frontend unit-test coverage, and an integration test that captures the final OpenAI prompt remain gaps; the latter would require a mockable OpenAI boundary and disposable PostgreSQL for the full route.
- 2026-08-13: Added optional per-section character-builder AI direction with backend trimming and a 2,000-character limit, persistent Identity/Appearance/Background/Experiences prompt controls, and active-section-only request wiring. Reduced server-side AI campaign-frame context to the five player-facing sections `pitch`, `tone_and_feel`, `themes`, `touchstones`, and `overview`, with legacy tone/touchstone aliases normalized and other root content excluded. Added focused whitelist unit coverage; browser and full route prompt-capture coverage remain unavailable.
# DaggerAdventure Feature Ledger

This document is the working map of DaggerAdventure features, their code paths, data flow, access rules, and validation status. It is an orientation aid for agents and developers. The source code, migrations, tests, and current user request remain authoritative when this ledger disagrees with implementation.

## Maintenance Contract

- Read this file before changing an existing feature or adding a feature that crosses the frontend and backend.
- Verify important claims in the referenced code before relying on them.
- After a feature change, update the affected entry, file paths, API contract, access rules, tests, and known limitations.
- Record uncertainty as `Needs verification`; do not turn an inferred behavior into a fact.
- Do not remove a feature entry because code is difficult to find. Mark it `Needs verification` or `Deprecated` and explain why.
- Keep this document focused on behavior and ownership. Do not copy large implementation details or generated output into it.

## Status Vocabulary

- **Implemented**: the main code path is present and confirmed in the current repository.
- **Partial**: some UI, API, persistence, or validation exists, but the end-to-end behavior is incomplete or intentionally limited.
- **Needs verification**: the repository contains related code, but the complete behavior or current production state has not been confirmed.
- **Deprecated**: retained for history or compatibility but should not receive new callers.

## System Map

| Layer | Responsibility | Primary paths |
|---|---|---|
| React client | Routes, pages, feature state, and API calls | [`frontend/src/routes/AppRoutes.jsx`](../frontend/src/routes/AppRoutes.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/`](../frontend/src/features/) |
| API client | Cookie-authenticated JSON requests and error unwrapping | [`frontend/src/api/client.js`](../frontend/src/api/client.js) |
| Rust API | Axum routes, auth middleware, validation, and response models | [`backend/src/routes/mod.rs`](../backend/src/routes/mod.rs), [`backend/src/routes/`](../backend/src/routes/) |
| Domain and persistence | Services, repositories, models, and access policy | [`backend/src/services/`](../backend/src/services/), [`backend/src/repository/`](../backend/src/repository/), [`backend/src/models/`](../backend/src/models/) |
| Database | PostgreSQL schema managed by SQLx migrations | [`backend/migrations/`](../backend/migrations/) |
| Deployment | Docker Compose, Kubernetes, nginx, Jenkins, and Argo CD | [`docker-compose.yml`](../docker-compose.yml), [`k8s/`](../k8s/), [`Jenkinsfile`](../Jenkinsfile) |

## Request and Persistence Flow

1. A React page calls a feature API module.
2. [`frontend/src/api/client.js`](../frontend/src/api/client.js) sends JSON with `credentials: 'include'`, so the authentication cookie is included.
3. Public auth routes are handled directly. Protected routes pass through `require_auth` in [`backend/src/middleware/auth_guard.rs`](../backend/src/middleware/auth_guard.rs).
4. Route handlers validate input, apply access and ownership rules, call repositories or services, and return JSON or the established `AppError` response.
5. The backend starts by connecting to PostgreSQL and applying pending SQLx migrations in [`backend/src/main.rs`](../backend/src/main.rs) and [`backend/src/lib.rs`](../backend/src/lib.rs).
6. The frontend represents the response in the feature page or store. Loading, empty, and error behavior must be verified in the touched component rather than assumed from the API name.

## Access Model

The canonical access levels are defined in [`backend/src/models/user.rs`](../backend/src/models/user.rs) and [`frontend/src/utils/permissions.js`](../frontend/src/utils/permissions.js):

| Level | Rank | Intended capability |
|---|---:|---|
| `nothing` | 0 | Authenticated account without player access |
| `player_only` | 1 | Character and player workflows |
| `adventure_maker` | 2 | Player workflows plus adventure and frame creation |
| `admin` | 3 | Administrative workflows and AI access |

Backend access checks use `require_at_least` and `require_ai_generation` in [`backend/src/middleware/access_guard.rs`](../backend/src/middleware/access_guard.rs). The frontend uses `ProtectedRoute` and the same rank ordering. Server authorization is authoritative; frontend restrictions are navigation and user-experience safeguards only.

## Feature Inventory

### Authentication and Account Management

- **Status:** Implemented; email verification and shared abuse controls are confirmed in the current route, service, repository, migration, and client paths.
- **Frontend:** [`frontend/src/pages/Auth/LoginPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/pages/Auth/LoginPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/pages/Auth/RegisterPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/pages/Auth/RegisterPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/pages/Auth/VerifyEmailPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/pages/Auth/VerifyEmailPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/account/SettingsPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/account/SettingsPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/api/authApi.js`](../frontend/src/api/authApi.js), [`frontend/src/store/authStore.js`](../frontend/src/store/authStore.js), [`frontend/src/routes/AppRoutes.jsx`](../frontend/src/routes/AppRoutes.jsx), [`frontend/src/routes/ProtectedRoute.jsx`](../frontend/src/routes/ProtectedRoute.jsx), [`frontend/nginx.conf`](../frontend/nginx.conf).
- **Backend:** [`backend/src/routes/mod.rs`](../backend/src/routes/mod.rs), [`backend/src/routes/auth.rs`](../backend/src/routes/auth.rs), [`backend/src/routes/users.rs`](../backend/src/routes/users.rs), [`backend/src/models/user.rs`](../backend/src/models/user.rs), [`backend/src/config.rs`](../backend/src/config.rs), [`backend/src/error.rs`](../backend/src/error.rs), [`backend/src/services/auth_service.rs`](../backend/src/services/auth_service.rs), [`backend/src/services/email_service.rs`](../backend/src/services/email_service.rs), [`backend/src/services/rate_limit.rs`](../backend/src/services/rate_limit.rs), [`backend/src/middleware/auth_guard.rs`](../backend/src/middleware/auth_guard.rs), [`backend/src/repository/user_repo.rs`](../backend/src/repository/user_repo.rs), [`backend/src/repository/verification_repo.rs`](../backend/src/repository/verification_repo.rs), [`backend/src/repository/rate_limit_repo.rs`](../backend/src/repository/rate_limit_repo.rs), [`backend/src/repository/adventure_repo.rs`](../backend/src/repository/adventure_repo.rs), [`backend/migrations/0021_add_email_verification_and_rate_limits.up.sql`](../backend/migrations/0021_add_email_verification_and_rate_limits.up.sql), [`backend/migrations/0021_add_email_verification_and_rate_limits.down.sql`](../backend/migrations/0021_add_email_verification_and_rate_limits.down.sql), [`backend/migrations/0022_add_email_verification_required.up.sql`](../backend/migrations/0022_add_email_verification_required.up.sql), [`backend/migrations/0022_add_email_verification_required.down.sql`](../backend/migrations/0022_add_email_verification_required.down.sql).
- **API:** `POST /api/auth/register` (`202` pending response; `400` validation, `429` rate limit, or `503` unavailable/failed delivery), `POST /api/auth/login` (`200` plus HTTP-only cookie; `401` invalid credentials, `403` required verification, or `429` rate limit), `POST /api/auth/verify-email` (`200` verified user; `400` invalid/expired/consumed token, or `429` rate limit), `POST /api/auth/resend-verification` (`202` generic response; `400` validation, `429` rate limit, or `503` unavailable/failed delivery), `POST /api/auth/logout` (`200` and expired cookie), and protected `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/auth/me` (`200`; unauthenticated `401`, verification-blocked `403`).
- **Behavior:** Registration returns `202` with a generic verification-pending response only after email delivery is configured, the user and hashed verification token commit atomically, and delivery accepts the message; unavailable or failed delivery returns a safe `503` and never claims success. Registration never issues a session cookie. New registrations explicitly set `email_verification_required=true`. Migration `0022_add_email_verification_required` defaults that flag to `false` for existing rows, preserves NULL `email_verified_at`, and grandfathers legacy accounts until a future explicit enforcement migration or admin operation changes the flag; it does not silently verify them or alter admin approval/access semantics. Verification tokens are cryptographically generated, stored only as SHA-256 hashes, expire after one hour, and are deleted on consumption. Resend inserts another hashed one-use token, retains every still-valid prior token, and removes at most 50 expired tokens for that user before insertion; delivery failure therefore cannot delete a previously usable link, and successful resend does not invalidate one. `VerifyEmailPage` reads the token from the URL fragment, immediately scrubs the URL, shares one request across React StrictMode effect setup/cleanup cycles, and ignores results after the page becomes inactive. Verification links pending adventure invites only after successful token consumption; registration no longer links them. Login and auth middleware enforce verification only when `email_verification_required` is true and the timestamp is NULL. Existing legacy accounts remain recoverable through resend once delivery is configured. Resend responses remain generic for unknown or already verified addresses. The verification page and successful verification API response send `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- **Abuse controls:** Registration, login, resend, and verification consumption use PostgreSQL-backed atomic fixed-window buckets keyed by scope plus a SHA-256 hash of normalized email and/or connection IP, so limits are shared across backend replicas without storing the raw identity in the bucket key. Rate-limited responses are `429` with `Retry-After`; buckets expire after 24 hours of inactivity and do not create permanent account lockouts. `TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS` is disabled by default. The bundled Kubernetes deployment enables it only for the explicitly configured private chain: [`nginx/templates/app.conf.template`](../nginx/templates/app.conf.template) overwrites `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Real-IP`, and [`argo/install-argocd.sh`](../argo/install-argocd.sh) configures ingress-nginx with `use-forwarded-headers=true`; this remains an operational trust assumption, so the ingress NodePort must stay private and the setting must not be reused with a pass-through proxy.
- **Email delivery:** [`backend/src/services/email_service.rs`](../backend/src/services/email_service.rs) is the backend-only provider boundary. `EMAIL_PROVIDER=disabled` is the safe default and fails registration closed with `503`; the bundled Kubernetes deployment intentionally keeps that limitation, so it cannot create new accounts through email verification. `EMAIL_PROVIDER=dev_file` is the only implemented delivery mode and writes a local append-only, untracked development outbox when `EMAIL_DEV_OUTBOX` and valid `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_BASE_URL` values are configured. `EMAIL_FROM` and the verification URL are validated as safe single-line values at startup and at the delivery boundary. Links use a fragment token, and no production provider implementation or credentials are configured in this repository, so production registration remains blocked until a provider is added. Delivery is attempted after the user/token transaction commits; a later failure leaves the unverified account and prior usable tokens recoverable through resend.
- **Deployment/docs:** [`k8s/backend/deployment.yaml`](../k8s/backend/deployment.yaml) keeps `EMAIL_PROVIDER=disabled` and enables proxy-header trust for the documented private chain; [`k8s/ingress.yaml`](../k8s/ingress.yaml) keeps the backend behind the ingress service; [`INSTALLATION.md`](../INSTALLATION.md) and [`README.md`](../README.md) document the legacy-account transition, local outbox, fail-closed production limitation, and proxy-header assumption. No production provider or credentials are present.
- **Behavior:** The existing admin approval contract remains unchanged: verification does not grant player access, and new accounts still default to `nothing` until approval.
- **Invariants:** Normalize email and validate names/passwords through [`backend/src/utils/validation.rs`](../backend/src/utils/validation.rs). Do not move the OpenAI key, auth secrets, or verification tokens into browser code. The legacy `auth_service::register` helper remains only for existing ignored PostgreSQL fixtures; the HTTP registration route uses `register_pending` and is the user-facing security boundary.
- **Test fixtures:** Ignored PostgreSQL protected-flow fixtures use [`backend/tests/common/fixtures.rs`](../backend/tests/common/fixtures.rs) and `register_verified`, which calls the legacy `auth_service::register` helper, explicitly sets only `email_verified_at`, and runs the post-verification pending-invite linking step; it does not exercise delivery-backed HTTP registration. [`backend/tests/auth_tests.rs`](../backend/tests/auth_tests.rs) retains a pending-registration case that verifies new users keep `email_verification_required=true` and cannot log in before verification. [`backend/tests/character_tests.rs`](../backend/tests/character_tests.rs) uses the same verified fixture for protected character flows.
- **Validation:** Database-free backend token/hash, expiry, limiter-key, retry calculation, validation/configuration, and disabled-delivery tests pass. Backend test targets compile without executing PostgreSQL tests; frontend lint/build pass. Browser coverage, email-provider integration, disposable-PostgreSQL route execution, HTTP `register_pending`/resend/verify flow execution, and live transition testing for pre-migration accounts remain gaps.

### Access Levels and Administration

- **Status:** Implemented; route tree and access helpers confirmed.
- **Frontend:** [`frontend/src/features/admin/AdminUsersPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/admin/AdminUsersPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/admin/AdminAuditPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/admin/AdminAuditPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/admin/adminApi.js`](../frontend/src/features/admin/adminApi.js).
- **Backend:** [`backend/src/routes/admin.rs`](../backend/src/routes/admin.rs), [`backend/src/repository/admin_repo.rs`](../backend/src/repository/admin_repo.rs), [`backend/src/models/admin.rs`](../backend/src/models/admin.rs).
- **API:** `GET /api/admin/users`, `PATCH /api/admin/users/:target_id/access-level`, `PATCH /api/admin/users/:target_id/approval`, `PATCH /api/admin/users/:target_id/ai-generation`, `GET /api/admin/access-audit`.
- **Behavior:** New registrations leave `access_level` at the existing database default, `nothing`, until an administrator reviews the account. Admins can list users with search, access-level filtering including a pending `nothing` filter, visible Accept/Refuse controls, and 25-item pagination. The dedicated admin-only approval operation locks the target and accepts only users whose current access is `nothing`; `approved: true` grants `player_only`, while `approved: false` leaves the pending account at `nothing`. Approval grants use the existing access audit event path; the separate general access-level endpoint retains its role-administration behavior and last-admin safeguards, as does the separate AI-generation access operation. After approval mutations, the captured search/filter/page query is refreshed only when its query identity and version are still active; a newer query remains authoritative. User-list fetches use a latest-request generation guard so out-of-order responses cannot overwrite newer users, totals, loading, or errors, and the latest failed request clears stale rows and totals. Approval failures refresh the still-active query when possible and keep the mutation error visible. Account bootstrap can promote the configured `ADMIN_EMAIL` at startup. No migration or new persistent setting was added; this reuses the existing access-level contract and adds only the approval API/request contract.
- **Invariants:** Do not rely on a frontend access check as authorization. Preserve the rank ordering and server-side admin checks. Refusing a pending account is non-destructive and does not delete or demote an elevated account; stale approval requests receive a conflict. Search and access-level filters are preserved across pagination and reset the page to 1 when changed.
- **Validation:** The frontend has no unit-test runner; focused browser coverage for the pending filter, visible Accept/Refuse controls, approval conflicts, confirmations, active-query refresh, out-of-order fetches, pagination, and visible mutation errors remains unavailable. No focused approval integration test was found, and browser or live PostgreSQL execution was not performed. Required static validation is frontend `npm run lint` and `npm run build`, backend `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo test --lib`, `cargo test --tests --no-run`, and `git diff --check`.

Browser, frontend unit-test, and live PostgreSQL coverage for loot normalization, supplied/transient rolls, filter interaction, responsive layout, retry states, and the catalog request remain unavailable; the inspected backend content tests cover book-shape validation, not Equipment-specific endpoint or rendering behavior.

A player first chooses an accessible adventure or the standalone option in the builder. A direct `?adventure=<id>` selection remains usable even while the adventure list is loading or when that ID is not returned by the list; list and frame-load failures are surfaced without destroying that selection, and stale frame responses cannot replace newer route state. The character model includes identity, appearance, class/subclass, ancestry/community, traits, experiences, background, family, connections, equipment, domain cards, level, advancements, and an optional portrait.

No migration or API request-shape change was added.

Keep character content compatible with the current content-book IDs. All character routes are authenticated and require `player_only` access; the vault list and deletion are owner-scoped, detail reads are available to the character owner or linked adventure creator, and character mutations remain owner-scoped. Character creation and adventure linking additionally require the adventure creator or an accepted member when an adventure is selected. Adventure selection, edit-mode linking, and frame context use the existing APIs and server-side membership/ownership rules; this guidance reconciliation changes no API, database schema, or access rule.

Adventure note deletion normalizes its former section in the same transaction, and note listing orders by section position, note position, and stable IDs. After successful note or section mutations, the adventure and character detail pages refetch the complete normalized note response with current-resource/request-generation guards; refresh failures remain visible with a retry action, and the note manager preserves dirty drafts while refreshed props arrive. A successful section deletion reports canonical current sections to NoteManager, so a superseded earlier refresh cannot turn the delete into failure or supply a pre-delete fallback; an unavailable or invalid post-delete list blocks the deleted section until a retry supplies a valid survivor, preventing later saves from falling back to the deleted section. This serializes concurrent creates, moves, deletes, and section reorders for the same parent without changing ownership or normalization semantics.

Player roster access requires an accepted membership or creator ownership, and the query joins only accepted members and selects only the nullable summary fields. Membership visibility excludes pending invitees from frame and character reads until acceptance. PostgreSQL `ON DELETE CASCADE` owns member/invite/notification/note/frame cleanup and `ON DELETE SET NULL` owns character preservation; do not reproduce these cascades in frontend state or bypass the server-side checks.

### Soundboards and GM Sound Library

- **Status:** Implemented; reusable owner-scoped library, named sources, board attachments, legacy sound compatibility, and persistent playback paths confirmed.
- **Frontend:** [`frontend/src/features/soundboards/SoundboardPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/soundboards/SoundboardPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/soundboards/SoundboardPage.module.css`](../frontend/src/features/soundboards/SoundboardPage.module.css), [`frontend/src/features/soundboards/soundboardApi.js`](../frontend/src/features/soundboards/soundboardApi.js), [`frontend/src/features/soundboards/soundboardStore.js`](../frontend/src/features/soundboards/soundboardStore.js), [`frontend/src/features/soundboards/SoundPlayer.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/soundboards/SoundPlayer.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/soundboards/SoundPlayer.module.css`](../frontend/src/features/soundboards/SoundPlayer.module.css), [`frontend/src/features/adventures/AdventureDetailPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/adventures/AdventureDetailPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/adventures/AdventureDetailPage.module.css`](../frontend/src/features/adventures/AdventureDetailPage.module.css), [`frontend/src/layouts/AppLayout.jsx`](../frontend/src/layouts/AppLayout.jsx).
- **Backend:** [`backend/src/routes/mod.rs`](../backend/src/routes/mod.rs), [`backend/src/routes/soundboards.rs`](../backend/src/routes/soundboards.rs), [`backend/src/repository/soundboard_repo.rs`](../backend/src/repository/soundboard_repo.rs), [`backend/src/models/soundboard.rs`](../backend/src/models/soundboard.rs), [`backend/migrations/0019_create_soundboards.up.sql`](../backend/migrations/0019_create_soundboards.up.sql), [`backend/migrations/0020_create_sound_library.up.sql`](../backend/migrations/0020_create_sound_library.up.sql), [`backend/migrations/0020_create_sound_library.down.sql`](../backend/migrations/0020_create_sound_library.down.sql).
- **Proxy and deployment documentation:** [`nginx/templates/app.conf.template`](../nginx/templates/app.conf.template), [`k8s/ingress.yaml`](../k8s/ingress.yaml), [`INSTALLATION.md`](../INSTALLATION.md), [`argo/install-argocd.sh`](../argo/install-argocd.sh).
- **API:** `GET/POST /api/sound-sources`, `PUT/DELETE /api/sound-sources/:source_id`, `GET/POST /api/sound-library`, `DELETE /api/sound-library/:track_id`, `GET /api/sound-library/:track_id/:kind`, `POST/DELETE /api/soundboards/:board_id/library/:track_id`; existing board and direct-sound endpoints remain supported.
- **Current UI behavior:** Add Track uses named-source attribution and no longer asks for creator or free-form source-credit fields. The persistent player supports Off/Song/Queue repeat modes, a hidden compact name-only state, and a seek track whose progress begins at the left edge. Library, board, and adventure sound cards provide centered artwork playback; the adventure Sounds tab also filters the selected board by track name, label, and named source.
- **Behavior:** Adventure makers can create tracks independently of boards using exactly one uploaded audio file or HTTP(S) audio URL, optional artwork upload/URL, up to 12 labels, creator/source credit, and an owner-selected named source. Named sources have owner-scoped names, website URLs, descriptions, and CRUD. Library tracks can attach to multiple owned boards through a link table without copying media; board counts and detail responses include both reusable attachments and legacy direct sounds. Shared-board readers can read attached media and see credits, while owner-only board/library/source mutations remain hidden in the UI and enforced server-side. Uploaded media is returned only through authenticated media endpoints. `SoundPlayer` remains owned by `AppLayout`; its module-level audio element, store state, and FIFO queue survive route changes, while the current-track link opens `/soundboards` without stopping playback. Native audio controls are not rendered; custom play/pause, seeking, queue removal, and queue clearing are provided, and natural end consumes the next queued track. Library and board cards expose Play now and Add to queue actions, preserving explicit duplicate additions. Adventure creators receive a creator-only Sounds tab that loads the existing board list first, requires an explicit board selection before showing tracks, and uses the existing board detail/media responses for play and queue actions; non-creators do not receive the tab. Detail responses use the `{ board, sounds }` shape expected by the page, and detail loads and mutation refreshes are guarded by the selected board and request generations; stale detail is cleared during selection changes and attachment controls remain unavailable until the detail matches the selection. Workspace board/source/library loads and local mutation refreshes use a generation guard so out-of-order responses cannot overwrite collections, selection, loading, or errors. Implicit workspace refreshes resolve selection from the current-selection ref at response time, so user changes remain authoritative over in-flight refreshes; explicit preferred IDs retain intentional create/delete selection. Deleting or refreshing named sources normalizes the track form's selected source. The outer HTTPS proxy and Kubernetes Nginx ingress allow a 64 MB request envelope, above the backend's 60 MiB multipart limit, preventing proxy-level 413 responses for supported uploads.
- **Final implementation details:** Per-file validation caps audio uploads at 50 MiB and artwork uploads at 5 MiB; the sound upload routes cap each multipart request at 60 MiB including overhead, while the outer nginx template, ingress annotation, and Argo installer configure 64 MB proxy limits. `SoundPlayer` invalidates pending `play()` attempts on pause, tracks the active attempt generation, and requires native `play` callbacks to match that generation, playback version/source, and unpaused audio before updating state. The FIFO queue assigns unique entry IDs so duplicate additions remain distinct; natural-end advancement consumes the head entry and stops when empty.
- **Invariants:** Sources, tracks, labels, and attachments are owner-scoped; shared boards expose reads only. Legacy `sounds` rows and their media/delete routes are preserved. Deleting a source nulls the named source while retaining track-level source credit. Database constraints enforce exactly one audio source and matching upload MIME metadata. Uploaded files must have a supported audio/image signature matching the declared MIME type; external URLs remain URL-validated only and are not fetched by this validation. Duplicate owner-scoped source names return a conflict without leaking database details. No shared/admin source catalog was added.
- **Validation:** Database-free backend unit tests cover the nested detail serialization contract, source trimming/bounds, parsed URL schemes and hosts, multi-label parsing and rejection, oversized metadata, upload signatures, and MIME mismatches. Required backend formatting, unit tests, and test compilation plus frontend lint/build and diff checks are the documented checks. Proxy configuration edits are checked with `git diff --check` and editor diagnostics; runtime Nginx/Kubernetes validation remains unavailable without starting deployment infrastructure. Browser coverage, frontend unit-test coverage, and disposable-PostgreSQL execution remain unavailable; workspace response ordering and source unique-violation behavior are covered by implementation/repository mapping but not browser/integration tests. No browser or frontend unit test currently verifies custom player interaction, route-preserved playback, FIFO natural-end advancement, queue mutations, or creator-only adventure board selection.

### Deployment and Operations

- **Status:** Implemented; configuration and pipeline paths documented, runtime state still environment-dependent.
- **Local runtime:** PostgreSQL through [`docker-compose.yml`](../docker-compose.yml), backend on port 8080, frontend Vite development server normally on port 5173.
- **Production runtime:** nginx and Certbot, Kubernetes manifests under [`k8s/`](../k8s/), Argo CD bootstrap under [`argo/`](../argo/), Jenkins pipeline in [`Jenkinsfile`](../Jenkinsfile).
- **Checks:** Backend `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo check`, and `cargo test`; frontend `npm run lint` and `npm run build`; Docker check targets documented in [`README.md`](../README.md). Jenkins' integration smoke test runs the current email-verification contract against disposable containers: health check, `202` registration through the development outbox, token verification, password login, and a protected `/api/hello` request. Each smoke-test network and PostgreSQL/backend container name is scoped to the build by a 16-character SHA-256 suffix derived from the Jenkins build identity, preventing concurrent builds from sharing fixed Docker resource names. Authentication calls use bounded failure behavior and do not retry `503`/`429` responses indefinitely.
- **Invariants:** Secrets remain outside committed files. Migrations run at backend startup. The smoke-test `EXIT` trap is installed before Docker resources are created and removes the build-scoped backend/PostgreSQL containers, network, and temporary email outbox on success or failure; the pipeline-level `post` cleanup repeats the Docker removal. The smoke-test stage and pipeline `post` cleanup derive the same 16-character SHA-256 suffix from `BUILD_TAG`, falling back identically to `jenkins-${JOB_NAME:-daggeradventure}-${BUILD_NUMBER:-unknown}` when `BUILD_TAG` is absent. The Jenkins promotion branch merges the fetched current `production` ref into the tested source commit before rewriting only the backend and frontend image fields; merge conflicts fail the promotion. Do not change deployment names, image paths, ports, or secret keys without checking Compose, Kubernetes, nginx, and Jenkins together.

- Email verification has no browser or frontend unit coverage for registration-pending, resend, token success/failure, login recovery, or protected-route redirects. No real email provider is configured; only the disabled default and local `dev_file` outbox boundary are implemented.
